user.title: Set up Fetch Latest File
user.description: This integration allows you to list the most recently modified files from a directory based on filename patterns, extensions, and minimum file size. Results are reported by actual file extension.

abort.already_configured: Fetch Latest File is already configured.

init.title: Fetch Latest File Options
init.description: Configure allowed search directories, scan limits, and cleanup of saved target results.

data_description.allowed_directories: Enter one directory per line. Prefer explicit roots limited to the directories your automations need. Leave blank to allow any readable directory.
data_description.max_scan_depth: Scan up to this many subdirectory levels (0-100). Zero searches only the top-level directory.
data_description.max_files_to_check: Check at most this many files per scan (1-100000). Directory watches are separately bounded by the same limit.
data_description.max_target_ids: Keep results for at most this many target IDs (1-100). The oldest results are removed first.
data_description.target_expiry_hours: Remove saved target results older than this many hours (1-168).

fetch.name: Fetch latest file
fetch.description: Fetches the most recent file that starts with the given filename in the specified directory, plus the latest match for each file extension. Optionally, filter by file extension and/or minimum file size.

directory.name: Directory
directory.description: The directory to search for files. The search is recursive and includes subdirectories.

filename.name: Filename prefix
filename.description: The beginning of the filename of the file to fetch. Case-insensitive.

extension.name: Extension
extension.description: Enter each extension separately, without the dot (for example, jpg and mp4). Leave empty to search all extensions. Reserved names, no_extension, and extensions starting with ext_ receive an extra ext_ prefix in results.

min_size.name: Minimum file size
min_size.description: Nonnegative decimal size, such as 1024, 1KB, 1MB, or 1.5M. Bare values or B mean bytes; K/KB, M/MB, and G/GB use powers of 1024, case-insensitively. Fractional bytes round up. Defaults to 0B.

target_id.name: Target ID
target_id.description: A unique identifier for this fetch operation. Use 1-64 letters, numbers, underscores, or hyphens. Service calls with different target_id values can run in parallel, while calls with the same target_id will execute sequentially to prevent conflicts. If not specified, uses 'default'.

wait_for_upload.name: Wait for upload
wait_for_upload.description: Select and pin one file per extension, optionally by position in a fresh upload sequence. Wait for writer-close notifications or observed stability. Later files never replace pinned uploads. Timeout completion is indicated in FetchStatus. Defaults to false.

timeout.name: Upload timeout
timeout.description: Maximum upload wait in seconds, starting when this target begins processing. At timeout, keep the same size-qualified pins. If the requested sequence position has not arrived, use its last size-qualified image. Ignored when upload waiting is disabled. Defaults to 30.

quiet_period.name: Quiet period
quiet_period.description: Seconds of unchanged file identity, size, and modification time needed for heuristic readiness. A paused upload can appear complete. Ignored when upload waiting is disabled. Defaults to 2.

fresh_extensions.name: Fresh extensions
fresh_extensions.description: A list of extensions requiring recent uploads when waiting. Entries ignore case, surrounding whitespace, and leading dots, and must be included in Extension after normalization. Selects the newest eligible file or waits for the next; with Burst position, selects from the latest qualifying sequence. Ignored when upload waiting is disabled. Defaults to an empty list.

freshness_window.name: Freshness window
freshness_window.description: Positive seconds before invocation allowed for recent filesystem updates. With Burst position, freshness checks the sequence's newest image, so the selected image may be older. Otherwise checks individual files. The cutoff stays fixed. Applies only when waiting with Fresh extensions. Defaults to 5.

burst_position.name: Burst position
burst_position.description: Select this position in the latest qualifying upload sequence for each Fresh extension. Use 1, 2, 3, or any positive whole number. Requires Fresh extensions; applies only when waiting. If the position never arrives, use the last size-qualified file from that sequence. Omit to retain ordinary fresh-file selection.

burst_gap.name: Burst gap
burst_gap.description: Positive seconds separating sequences by filesystem timestamps when files are first observed. Later writes reset the idle timer without bridging sequence gaps. A gap of at least this duration starts a new sequence; this much inactivity closes it. Applies only with Burst position while waiting. Defaults to 5.

lookback_window.name: Lookback window
lookback_window.description: Positive seconds of history before invocation searched for a sequence start. This boundary stays fixed. If the sequence start is outside this window or obscured by scan limits, return no file for that extension. Applies only with Burst position while waiting. Defaults to 60.

unavailable.message: Fetch Latest File is unavailable. Set up or reload the integration and try again.
